selection_rule: lowest validation window MAE (models fit on train subjects only)
final_fit_data: train subjects only (validation used for selection, not merged into training)
nan_handling: feature NaNs (single-fix windows: displacement/path/derived speed; first window of a track: lag_*) are passed natively to RF (sklearn>=1.4) and XGBoost

baselines.baseline_linear_distance: steps = 1.4385 steps/m x (GPS speed_mean x 5 s); k = median ratio over train windows with distance >= 0.5 m

alignment_decision: H0: treat positions.ms and steps.ms as the same signalStart clock; apply NO per-track or global lag shift; do not re-base positions by testStart.
alignment_confidence: moderate (clock identity supported; sub-window offsets of a few seconds cannot be excluded)

step_handling_decision.rule: Treat the counter as cumulative with out-of-order delivery of rows inside one reporting batch: cum(T) = running maximum of steps over rows with ms<=T (rows ordered by ms); window increment = cum(T_end) - cum(T_start). Never clip individual diffs; report the window-level net change. Rows at identical ms are kept (no dedup needed: running max is order-independent).
step_handling_decision.known_limitation: A window boundary falling inside a batch can credit up to the batch's max decrease (<=4 steps) to one window and take it back in the next; the net over the track is exact.
step_handling_decision.observed_pattern: All decreases lie inside one endDate batch (rows with identical endDate, ms differing by 0-12 ms): rows of a batch are delivered out of order, not counter resets or corrections. Exception in kind: 14_4 has one row with steps==0 inside a batch (-6) and 14_9 a -10 jump inside a batch; both recover within the batch. Sorting by ms (stable) does not fix them, sorting by (endDate, steps) fixes all but 1 event.
step_handling_decision.metadata_reconciliation_exceptions: 5_7 (metadata totSteps is 1 below the last value) and 14_7 (running max is 1 above the last-row value that equals totSteps); 1 step each
step_handling_decision.before_first_row: counter taken as 0 before the first row (first row already holds several steps)

window_target: cum(T_end)-cum(T_start), cum = running max of steps counter (monotonicity decision)
